newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks amble to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks amble to higher close.

text.p: Australian shares closed higher on Monday, the market carried to a firmer finish in light choppy trade by a modest rally staged in CRA and mild gains amongst most of the others.
The All Ordinaries index gained 7.3 points to 2,482.6.
Most of the major miners posted mild gains, although in the leaders CRA was the standout after shares in its dual-listed sibling, RTZ Plc, gained ground in London.
CRA scrip gained 15 cents to A$19.09 (US$14.84).
"Most of the miners have had a reasonable day," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage, highlighting CRA's leading role in the day's performance.
"CRA is what has held it together but BHP was all over the place," he said, pointing to choppy trade in the bellwether.
Other players echoed similar sentiments and suggested the looming options expiry on Thursday as one possible reason for the mild volatility of the market leader.
"We have got options expiry on Thursday and you often see the leaders pushed about in the run up to that," said a Brisbane broker.
MIM Holdings also featured in the resources, riding six cents higher to A$1.87 on the back of the stronger metals prices offshore.
Drug developer Biota Holdings rose 80 cents to A$4.10 after the company said clinical trials of its anti-influenza drug, Zanamivir, would begin in Australia in May.
Results continued, with aluminium producer Comalco gaining eight cents to A$6.90 despite a net loss for the 1996 year of A$16.8 million, on a joint venture basis.
QBE Insurance shares were five cents lower at A$6.39 after reporting a half year net profit of A$85.4 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
